title: EKSU FMS 312 - ENTREPRENEURIAL STUDY II | Practice Bank

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a feasibility study in entrepreneurship?

options.A: To secure immediate funding for a project
options.B: To assess the practicality and viability of a proposed business venture
options.C: To determine the final selling price of products
options.D: To conduct a post-launch performance review

questions.stem: In the context of a feasibility report, what does "viability" refer to?

options.A: The technical ease of implementing the project
options.B: The potential for the project to be profitable and sustainable
options.C: The number of competitors in the market

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key consideration when selecting a source of short-term financing?

options.A: The company's long-term debt-to-equity ratio
options.B: The interest rate and other costs associated with the financing
options.C: The potential for future expansion of the business

questions.stem: What does the term "net 30" in a credit term signify?

options.A: The customer has 30 days from the invoice date to pay the full amount without penalty
options.B: A 30% discount is offered if paid within 30 days
options.C: The payment is due immediately upon receipt of goods
options.D: A late payment fee of 30% will be applied after 30 days

questions.stem: If a company offers credit terms of "2/15, net 30", what is the discount percentage offered for early payment?
In the credit terms "2/15, net 30", how many days does the customer have to pay the full invoice amount if they do not take the discount?

options.A: 15 days
options.B: 2 days
options.C: 30 days

questions.stem: What is the fundamental purpose of trade credit?

options.A: To provide long-term capital for business expansion
options.B: To allow customers to purchase goods or services and pay for them later
options.C: To finance the purchase of fixed assets

questions.stem: Which of the following is a category of trade credit?

options.A: Bank overdrafts
options.B: Leasing agreements
options.C: Supplier credit

questions.stem: Agidingbi Consult Ltd. pledges its receivables to GTBank. What is this arrangement commonly known as?

options.A: Factoring
options.B: Leasing
options.C: Underwriting

questions.stem: In the scenario of Agidingbi Consult Ltd., GTBank advances up to 75 percent of the face value of the receivable. What does this percentage represent?

options.A: The total cost of financing
options.B: The loan-to-value ratio
options.C: The processing charge

questions.stem: What is the interest rate charged by GTBank for financing receivables if the prime rate is 12% and the advance is at 4% over the prime rate?
What are the processing charges levied by GTBank on all receivables pledged by Agidingbi Consult Ltd.?

Agidingbi Consult Ltd. maintains the practice of borrowing the maximum amount possible. This indicates a desire to utilize leverage. What is the maximum percentage of the face value of receivables they can borrow?
If Agidingbi Consult Ltd. has average monthly sales of N25,000.00k and a two-month credit term, what is their average receivable balance?
Calculate the effective annual interest rate (cost) of a cash discount of 2/15, net 30. (Assume 360 days in a year).

options.A: Approximately 24.5%
options.B: Approximately 49.0%
options.C: Approximately 12.2%

questions.stem: Calculate the effective annual interest rate (cost) of a cash discount of 3/10, net 60. (Assume 360 days in a year).

options.A: Approximately 18.4%
options.B: Approximately 36.8%
options.C: Approximately 27.6%

questions.stem: What is a "Term Loan"?

options.A: A loan repaid over a specific period with a fixed schedule of payments
options.B: A loan that can be repaid at any time without penalty
options.C: A loan secured by physical assets only
options.D: A loan with an interest rate that fluctuates daily

questions.stem: Bonds represent a form of:

options.A: Equity financing
options.B: Debt financing
options.C: Grant funding

questions.stem: What distinguishes Preferred Stock from Common Stock?

options.A: Preferred stockholders have voting rights, while common stockholders do not.
options.B: Preferred stockholders have a claim on assets and dividends that is senior to common stockholders.
options.C: Common stockholders receive fixed dividends, while preferred stockholders do not.
options.D: Preferred stock is always a debt instrument.

questions.stem: Common Stockholders are typically the:

options.A: First to be repaid in case of liquidation
options.B: Owners of the company with residual claims on assets and earnings
options.C: Holders of a fixed maturity debt instrument

questions.stem: What is a Convertible Bond?

options.A: A bond that can be exchanged for cash at a predetermined price
options.B: A bond that can be converted into shares of the issuing company's common stock
options.C: A bond with an interest rate that is fixed for its entire life
options.D: A bond that is guaranteed by a third party

questions.stem: What is the main benefit of leasing as a financing option?

options.A: Ownership of the asset at the end of the lease term
options.B: Significant tax deductions on the asset's purchase price
options.C: Preservation of working capital by avoiding large upfront outlays
options.D: The ability to sell the asset at any time

questions.stem: What is a significant disadvantage of leasing as a financing option?

options.A: The lessee gains full ownership of the asset
options.B: The total cost of leasing can be higher than purchasing the asset over its lifetime
options.C: The lessor handles all maintenance costs
options.D: It provides immediate equity in the asset

questions.stem: The "contents of a good feasibility report" would typically include:

options.A: A detailed marketing plan and sales forecasts
options.B: Financial projections and analysis
options.C: Technical specifications of the equipment to be used

questions.stem: Which of the following is a crucial step in the conduct of a feasibility study?

options.A: Securing the final loan approval
options.B: Conducting a market analysis
options.C: Hiring the entire workforce

questions.stem: A feasibility study aims to determine if a project is:

options.A: Socially acceptable
options.B: Environmentally friendly
options.C: Technologically possible, financially viable, and operationally manageable

questions.stem: The "benefit of a good feasibility report" includes:

options.A: Providing a clear roadmap for project implementation
options.B: Identifying potential risks and challenges
options.C: Supporting funding applications by demonstrating viability

questions.stem: What does the term "net 60" in credit terms indicate?

options.A: The customer has 60 days to claim a discount
options.B: The full payment is due within 60 days from the invoice date
options.C: A 60% penalty is applied after 60 days
options.D: The discount is valid for 60 days

questions.stem: Which type of trade credit involves goods or services being supplied on credit by a vendor to a buyer?

options.A: Bank loans
options.B: Leasing
options.C: Supplier credit

questions.stem: In the context of financing based on receivables, what is a common arrangement?

options.A: Issuing long-term bonds
options.B: Factoring or pledging receivables
options.C: Obtaining a mortgage

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a feasibility study?

options.A: To manage day-to-day operations
options.B: To explore the potential success of a new venture before significant investment
options.C: To set the company's dividend policy

questions.stem: When considering short-term financing, which factor is most critical for a business operating on tight margins?

options.A: The length of the repayment term
options.B: The administrative complexity of the application process
options.C: The cost of financing (interest rates, fees)
options.D: The collateral requirements for long-term assets

questions.stem: In the credit term "3/10 net 60," what is the period during which the discount is available?

options.A: 3 days
options.B: 10 days
options.C: 60 days

questions.stem: If Agidingbi Consult Ltd. pledged all its receivables, it means they have:

options.A: Sold their receivables to the bank
options.B: Used their receivables as collateral for a loan
options.C: Transferred ownership of their receivables to the bank without recourse
options.D: Both A and B are possible depending on the agreement

questions.stem: The "prime rate" is a benchmark interest rate typically used by banks for:

options.A: Loans to individual consumers
options.B: Loans to the most creditworthy corporate customers
options.C: Government borrowing

questions.stem: What does it mean for a company to "maintain the practice of borrowing the maximum amount possible" on its receivables?

options.A: They are prioritizing debt repayment
options.B: They are seeking to maximize the immediate liquidity from their receivables
options.C: They are avoiding all forms of external financing
options.D: They are focusing on reducing their accounts payable

questions.stem: The cost to the buyer of a cash discount is essentially the:

options.A: Interest paid on the full invoice amount
options.B: Opportunity cost of not taking the discount
options.C: Processing fee charged by the supplier

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a category of trade credit?

options.A: Open account credit
options.B: Installment credit
options.C: Revolving credit

questions.stem: What is the fundamental nature of bonds issued by a company?

options.A: They represent ownership in the company.
options.B: They represent a loan made to the company.
options.C: They are a form of government subsidy.
options.D: They are a contract for future services.

questions.stem: Preferred stock typically offers dividends that are:

options.A: Variable and dependent on company profits
options.B: Fixed and paid before common stock dividends
options.C: Tax-deductible for the company
options.D: Paid only if the company issues new stock

questions.stem: What is the primary right of common stockholders?

options.A: To receive a fixed dividend payment
options.B: To vote on company matters and elect the board of directors
options.C: To have their investment repaid on a specific date
options.D: To have a senior claim on company assets

questions.stem: What is a key advantage of a Term Loan for a business?

options.A: It provides immediate access to funds without any repayment obligation.
options.B: The repayment schedule is fixed, allowing for predictable budgeting.
options.C: It can be recalled by the lender at any time.
options.D: It does not require any interest payments.

questions.stem: What is the significance of a "good feasibility report" for an entrepreneur?

options.A: It guarantees project success regardless of market conditions.
options.B: It helps in making informed decisions about whether to proceed with a project.
options.C: It replaces the need for a business plan.
options.D: It automatically secures all necessary permits.

questions.stem: The steps required for conducting a feasibility study typically involve:

options.A: Identifying the project idea and defining its scope
options.B: Conducting market, technical, financial, and organizational analyses
options.C: Evaluating the risks and proposing mitigation strategies

questions.stem: If a bank advances 75% of the face value of receivables at an interest rate of 4% over prime, and the prime rate is 12%, what is the effective interest rate on the advanced amount?
What does "net 30" in credit terms mean for the customer?

options.A: They can pay in 30 installments.
options.B: They have 30 days to pay the full amount without incurring a penalty.
options.C: They receive a 30% discount if paid within 30 days.

questions.stem: Which type of trade credit is characterized by goods being delivered with an expectation of future payment by the buyer?

options.A: Leasing
options.B: Factoring
options.C: Supplier credit

questions.stem: What is the main function of trade credit in a business context?

options.A: To provide long-term investment capital
options.B: To facilitate sales by offering customers payment flexibility
options.C: To cover employee salaries

questions.stem: In the context of a feasibility study, the "technical feasibility" assesses:

options.A: The market demand for the product or service.
options.B: The availability and cost of necessary technology and resources.
options.C: The financial profitability of the project.

questions.stem: If a company pledges its receivables to a bank for financing, and the bank advances 75% of the face value, what happens to the remaining 25%?

options.A: It is immediately paid to the company.
options.B: It is retained by the bank as profit.
options.C: It is the company's equity in the receivables, and the company may receive it after the bank is repaid.
options.D: It is forfeited by the company.
